Day 1
From Hotel: 12 min → Universal Epic Universe
1. Universal Epic Universe
Universal's fourth Orlando gate and the first all-new major American theme park in a generation. Five worlds — Celestial Park, Super Nintendo World, Isle of Berk, Dark Universe and the Wizarding World's Ministry of Magic — radiate from a garden hub crowned by the glowing Chronos portal.

Day 2
From Hotel: 27 min → Magic Kingdom
1. Magic Kingdom
Walt Disney World's original park and the most-visited theme park on Earth. Cinderella Castle anchors six lands of classic dark rides, runaway-train mountains and daily parades, and the day closes with fireworks over Main Street, U.S.A. Arrive by ferry or monorail — the lagoon crossing is part of the show.

Day 3
From Hotel: 19 min → EPCOT
1. EPCOT
Walt Disney World's second park, built around the geodesic Spaceship Earth sphere. World Discovery and World Nature cover science and major rides including Guardians of the Galaxy: Cosmic Rewind; World Showcase presents eleven countries around a 1.3-mile lagoon of pavilions, food, and live entertainment.

Local Tastes
Butterbeer
The Wizarding World's signature drink — a butterscotch-and-shortbread cream soda invented for Universal Orlando and poured cold, frozen or hot. Orlando is where it was first served anywhere on Earth.
The Wizarding World of Harry Potter
Dole Whip
Pineapple soft-serve with a cult following, a Disney-parks tradition for decades — the Magic Kingdom's Adventureland stand is its most famous home. Order it as a float, swirled into pineapple juice.
Aloha Isle
Cuban Sandwich
Florida's pressed classic — roast pork, ham, Swiss, pickles and mustard on toasted Cuban bread. Orlando's large Cuban and Puerto Rican communities keep the standard high far beyond Tampa and Miami.
Black Bean Deli · Zaza New Cuban Diner
Key Lime Pie
Florida's official state pie — tart key-lime custard in a graham crust under hand-whipped cream. Orlando's scratch bakeries squeeze fresh limes daily.
Sister Honey's · Charlie's Bakery and Creamery
Gator Bites
Fried alligator tail nuggets — a Central Florida swamp-country staple, mildly sweet and best with a squeeze of lime and remoulade. Eat them yards away the real thing at Gatorland.
Pearl's Good Eats · Café Tu Tu Tango

Day Trips by Train
Winter Park · 26 min
Orlando's elegant old-money neighbor — brick-paved Park Avenue boutiques and sidewalk cafés, the Morse Museum's unmatched Tiffany-glass collection, and a pontoon cruise through canals linking the chain of lakes. SunRail runs weekdays only.
book at: SunRail or Omio
West Palm Beach · 2 hr
Brightline's smooth intercity run ends steps off Clematis Street — palm-lined waterfront, the Norton Museum of Art, and a quick bridge-hop over to Palm Beach's Worth Avenue. Hourly departures make a long Atlantic-coast day realistic.
book at: Brightline or Omio

Heads Up
Epic Universe — Date-Specific Tickets
Admission is sold by calendar date and popular dates sell out — walk-up entry is not guaranteed.
Magic Kingdom — Late Close Shifts by Date
The park closes 10:00pm some nights and 11:00pm others, shifting date by date through the season.
Worth Knowing

Citrus Notes

This trip spans the two bookends of American theme-park design. Magic Kingdom perfected the hub-and-spoke — one castle, six lands, every sightline managed. Epic Universe is the first ground-up rethink in a generation: its hub is a garden, and its lands hide behind portals, invisible until you step through. Walking both in 48 hours is a masterclass in how the craft evolved across half a century.

The hotel's neighborhood is named for Philip Phillips, the citrus baron whose groves once covered these hills. His company pioneered flash pasteurization, which made orange juice drinkable year-round and put Florida citrus on every American breakfast table. Restaurant Row now grows on his old grove land — which feels like a fair trade.
